verdicts.reason: X measures evidence of a standing relationship with the agency (meetings, pilots, named officials) while Y measures structural conformity to the notice's requested topics, and a first-time commenter can mirror the notice perfectly with no relationship cues.
Citing CFR parts and sections is a formatting/specificity cue that a comment can display without ever contesting authority, and an ultra vires argument can be made without a single CFR pin cite.

X requires platform-emission residue (trailing docket line, vendor mail headers, template slotting) in addition to the address tail, so the very common form letter that carries only a bare name-city-ZIP sign-off scores near the top on Y and only mid-range on X.

Emotional intensity and first-hand operational testimony are orthogonal: a dispassionate operator can describe practice in flat register, and an outraged commenter can have no stake in the regulated activity.

Both score agency-directed praise, gratitude, or commendation of staff and process, with matching zero anchors of no praise language; the only gap is X's explicit exclusion of the ritual opening thanks, which Y also implicitly discounts by requiring unprompted praise.

Both score the submitter's self-credentialing through quantified organizational scale (members, assets, employees, market share, reach), with essentially the same cue list and the same zero anchor of no scale claim.
Y is a conjunctive rhetorical structure (praise, then acknowledgment, then a narrow ask) that explicitly scores 0 for uniformly supportive comments, exactly the case where X scores 10.
Both name adversarial legal-brief framing built on statutory conflict, plain-text mandates, absence of agency discretion, and legal jeopardy or remedy, and would fire on the same submissions.

Both score coalition or membership breadth deployed as a standing claim, with near-identical zero anchors of an unaffiliated individual voice; the divergent class (bare endorsement of an ally's filing with no named partners or figures) is a small share of the distribution.

X is scoped to OCR/scan garbling and treats clean born-digital text as 0, whereas Y also scores email-routing debris and portal residue, so the large class of forwarded-email comments with intact routing headers but clean prose scores high on Y and 0 on X.
The two instructions enumerate nearly the same figures (members, employees, assets, customers, market share, operational reach) for the same construct of foregrounded institutional scale.

X scores adversarial posture and imputation of bad faith regardless of legal form, so a polite, technically framed statutory-conflict brief scores high on Y and mid-range on X, while an angry non-legal rant scores 10 on X and 0 on Y.
Both require self-generated monetary compliance-cost figures with a stated basis and both score 0 for no numbers.
Both score whether a concrete, implementable alternative regulatory design is set out, with 0 for mere objection.
Both score grounding in regulatory history — prior rules, earlier filings and amendments, pilots, waivers, agency precedent — against the same zero anchor of treating the proposal as freestanding.
Both score visible ingestion artifacts of every kind (OCR corruption, duplicated or corrupted headers, raw email routing, stray page numbers, malformed spacing) with 0 for cleanly rendered prose.
